event_detail: After the task is done, the robot picks up the pot (not a task object) and carries it onto the left burner, pressing it against the kettle that is already sitting there; the kettle gets pushed or rotated.
evidence: At 40.0 s the kettle stands upright on the large left burner with a blue flame under it, and the gripper is at the pot on the right side of the stove. At 41.6-43.2 s the pot is lifted and carried left (right shoulder view; the wrist camera shows the pot rim filling the view and the kettle on the blue flame just beyond it). At 44.8 s the pot is right against the kettle on the left burner. In the left shoulder view the kettle's handle, edge-on at 43.2 s, now shows as a loop, so the kettle has been rotated or tilted by the contact. At 44.8 s the kettle still appears to be on the left burner and blue flame is still visible under it, so both stages still hold, but the extra pot motion risks knocking the kettle off. Uncertain how far the kettle has moved, because the arm partly hides it.
